sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1 (notes/hooks.md), growth of the UFLPA Entity List from the version in force before Doc 2's update to Doc 6's version. Medium target, hard welcome (no Easy slot, user 2026-10-09). Platform: rev 0 measured "In band — Easy tier", Low 1/5, and rev 1 "Too hard", 0/15 (## Platform validation); rev 2 is the one focused repair for rev 1's distinct failure (its bare date read as a typo); no platform result on rev 2 yet.
- Dependency plan: Doc 2 L23 (update as of November 25, 2024), L77 (supersedes the November 1, 2024 list), L21 and L77-110 (five (ii) and twenty-five (v) additions), L160 (Daqo first listed June 2022), L164 (no removals), L165 (107). Doc 6 L76 (list as of August 3, 2026), L182 (187). The November 1 version was in force on November 15; its size 107 - (5 + 25 - 1) = 78; growth 187 - 78 = 109; 109 / 78 = 139.74%.
- Universe: the 30 named additions of the November 25, 2024 update, each checked by script against Doc 2's own (i), (ii) and (v) lists (2026-10-09): only Xinjiang Daqo New Energy also sits on another sub-list ((i), L177); the five (ii) additions are on no other list and the other 24 (v) additions are on no other list. Cross-check of the printed totals (doc-map shared ground): Doc 2's lists hold 9 + 39 + 72 = 120 placements and 13 repeat appearances (XPCC twice more; Baoding LYSZD, Hetian Haolin, Hetian Taida, Hoshine, Daqo, Junggar on (i) and (v); Hefei Bitland, two Lop County entries, No. 4 VSETC, Tengxiang on (ii) and (v)), 120 - 13 = 107 as printed. The same counting gives Doc 4's 144 (= 107 + 37, its 35 (v) additions including the already listed Aksu Huafu and Ashele Copper) and Doc 6's 187 (= 144 + 43), so the printed totals count each entity once and the November 1 version held 78.
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only document that names the November 1, 2024 version or the November 2024 update (searched "November 1, 2024", "87391", "Western Gold", "Daqo"); Doc 4 starts from the November 25, 2024 list (L80) and Doc 6 from the January 15, 2025 list (L76), so without Doc 2 the count on November 15, 2024 is unknowable from the bundle. Doc 6 is the only source of the August 3, 2026 count (Doc 4's 144 is the latest otherwise). Doc 4 is not needed (the route 187 - 78 skips it) and is not marked. Measured on rev 0, whose documents and dependency rev 1 keeps: the platform's Document check found both marked documents needed ("Needed document 2 ✓" twice, 78.1% and an unfinished answer; "Needed document 6 ✓" twice, 84.6% and a note that no August 3, 2026 update was provided), and the closed-book check answered 84.6% from a remembered "about 78 entities on November 1, 2024" and a guessed 144 for 2026. The local removal probe without Doc 2 (## Blind solve) said "not answerable" and forced the gold at p 0.3 from memory. Stated risk: recall of the 2024 counts, which the platform's checks did not turn into a reach.
- Selected-lever checks: Same series, right edition: no document prints a count for November 15, 2024; the version then in force is the one Doc 2 superseded (published November 1, 2024), and Doc 2's 107 applies only from November 25 (wrong route 74.8%). Who belongs where: Xinjiang Daqo is a (v) addition that was already on the (i) list (wrong route 142.9%). Calculate across documents: Doc 2's base with Doc 6's end count.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Look-alike measure, Takes the wrong line item): Doc 2 L21's sub-list additions (5 + 25 = 30) taken as entities new to the list: base 107 - 30 = 77, (187 - 77) / 77 = 142.857% -> 142.9%; measured: 4 of 5 low attempts on rev 0 and, on rev 1, 3 low and 3 medium attempts (every attempt that placed November 15 in the November 1 version) gave 142.9% this way. Mode 2 (Wrong year or edition, Uses the wrong period or date): Doc 2 L165's 107 (as of November 25, 2024) taken as the count on November 15: (187 - 107) / 107 = 74.766% -> 74.8%; measured on rev 1, whose bare "November 15, 2024" all five high attempts, two medium and two low read as a typo for November 25 (74.8%); rev 2's "the list in force on" states that the date is meant and the in-force version must be found. Considered and not declared: Doc 4's 144 taken as the latest count, (144 - 78) / 78 = 84.6% (the closed-book answer), which the question's August 3, 2026 date rules out; both slips together, (144 - 107) / 107 = 34.6%.
- Calculation verification: Python Fractions 2026-10-09: 107 - (5 + 25 - 1) = 78; 187 - 78 = 109; 109/78 = 1.3974358974... -> 139.74% -> 139.7% (one decimal). Wrong routes: 110/77 = 1.4285714 -> 142.9%; 80/107 = 0.7476636 -> 74.8%; 66/78 = 0.8461538 -> 84.6%; 37/107 = 0.3457944 -> 34.6%. No input rounding: every input is an exact count. 139.744% sits 0.006 below the 139.75 boundary, so only early rounding of the ratio (1.40, giving 140.0%) moves it; no alternate input lands on 139.7%.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document states a percentage or count change of the list, a count for any date between November 1 and November 25, 2024, or 109; "November 15" is printed nowhere (Doc 1's filing stamp "11-15-24" belongs to the DOL rule). The page overview gives Doc 2 "5 entities added to section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii) list · 25 entities added to section 2(d)(2)(B)(v) list" (the 30 route) and Doc 6 "43 new entities"; it states neither 107, 187 nor 78. Shortest valid route: place November 15 between Doc 2's November 1 supersession and its November 25 update, back out the update's new entities (noticing Daqo), take Doc 6's 187, divide.
- Precision/readings: "UFLPA-listed entities" is the documents' "listed entities" (Doc 2 L61); "grow ... by what percentage" is relative change on the November 15 base; one decimal stated. Placements instead of entities would need sub-list counts no document prints and is not what "number of ... entities" means. On November 15, 2024 the version published November 1 was in force: Doc 2 supersedes it directly and dates its own list "as of November 25, 2024", and DHS publishes every revision as a Federal Register appendix (Doc 2 L35, L62), so no other change fell in between. On August 3, 2026, Doc 6's version "as of August 3, 2026". Any start date from November 1 to November 24, 2024 gives the same base; November 15 is printed nowhere, so the solver has to place it, and "the list in force on" says the date is deliberate (rev 1's bare date was read as a typo).
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json); D05's omitted Annex A graphics are irrelevant (no UFLPA content).
- Style/set review: 27 words, no em-dash. Sibling sketch i02 (entities listed when DOL published its H-2B NPRM, 78) is closed: the closed-book check on rev 0 recalled "about 78 entities on November 1, 2024", so a bare 78 gold could be reached without the documents.

Step 1's added "15" is printed in Doc 2 ("May 15, 2020").
- Revision history: rev 1 (2026-10-09) answers rev 0's difficulty result, "In band — Easy tier", Low 1/5 (Run 1, Version 95fd92): 4 of 5 low-model attempts fell for the Daqo trap (142.9%), and every attempt found the base edition by matching the question's "November 1, 2024" to Doc 2's supersession sentence. Rev 1 asks from November 15, 2024, a date no document prints, so the base edition must be placed in time (Doc 2's 107 dates from November 25), adding the edition trap to the Daqo trap without changing the gold (139.7%), the documents or the evidence beyond one added quote (Doc 2's "updated as of November 25, 2024"). Rev 0 (tested_sha256 2917dbde...) stays on record below. Rev 2 (2026-10-09) answers rev 1's "Too hard" (Low 0/5 · Medium 0/5 · High 0/5, Run 2, Version 4200aa): every high attempt and two medium and two low attempts took the bare "November 15, 2024" for a typo of November 25 and used 107 (74.8%); the Coach misread the base as unavailable. Rev 2 asks from "the list in force on November 15, 2024", keeping the date (so the in-force version must still be found) while stating that it is meant; the reasoning's Step 8 follows the wording; gold, documents, evidence and failure modes are unchanged. sections.question: To one decimal place, by what percentage did the number of UFLPA-listed entities grow from the list in force on November 15, 2024 to August 3, 2026?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source fact (Doc 2, dates and appendix 1): the November 2024 notice announces the UFLPA Entity List "updated as of November 25, 2024" and supersedes the list published in the Federal Register on November 1, 2024, so on November 15, 2024 the November 1 version was still in force. The list as of November 25, 2024 specifies "One hundred and seven entities" (107).

Step 2. Source fact (Doc 2, summary and appendix 1): the November 25, 2024 update adds five entities (5) to the section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii) list and twenty-five entities (25) to the section 2(d)(2)(B)(v) list, and no removals are made.

Step 3. Source fact (Doc 2, Xinjiang Daqo New Energy paragraph and the 2(d)(2)(B)(i) list): one of the twenty-five (v) additions, Xinjiang Daqo New Energy Co., Ltd., "was first listed on the UFLPA Entity List, pursuant to Section 2(d)(2)(B)(i), in June 2022" and still appears on the (i) list, so it was already on the November 1, 2024 version. None of the other additions appears on another sub-list.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): sub-list additions in the November 25, 2024 update: 5 + 25 = 30.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): entities new to the list in that update, leaving out Xinjiang Daqo: 30 - 1 = 29.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): entities on the November 1, 2024 version, still in force on November 15, 2024: 107 - 29 = 78.

Step 7. Source fact (Doc 6, appendix 1): the UFLPA Entity List as of August 3, 2026 specifies "One hundred and eighty-seven entities" (187).

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): growth in listed entities from the list in force on November 15, 2024 to the August 3, 2026 list: 187 - 78 = 109.

Step 9. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): growth as a share of the November 15, 2024 count, converted to percent and rounded to one decimal place: 109 / 78 = 139.7%.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Look-alike measure: Doc 2's five plus twenty-five sub-list additions include Xinjiang Daqo, listed since June 2022, so only 29 were new; counting 30 gives a 77 base and 142.9%. Wrong edition: Doc 2's 107 dates from November 25, after November 15; as the base it gives 74.8%.
